## Reval: expected steamers and further transport capacity

**Sources on this page:** p213 A1, p213 A2, p213 A3. [Concise case study](../naval/reval_steamer_notice.md).

<a id="edition-cases-naval-reval-steamer-notice-reval-expected-steamers-and-further-transport-capacity"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs p213 A1–A3 (PDF p216), **23 November 1918**; published `Nov22-24` key, unchanged. [Inputs](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/inputs.json), [exact certificates](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/certificates.json), [method](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/README.md).

The header reads `KOW v LP (06.20 p.m., November 23rd); FUER RVA 20.00 (23/11) 3 TLE`. Its stated receipt precedes the origin time on the same printed date; the discrepancy is preserved. These parts belong to the lower, 23 November section, separately from the 22 November medical continuation above them.

The message reports arrangements for two steamers to serve troops and provisions at Reval by the end of November, with more tonnage and raw-material transport to follow. Contemporary shipping records now support three separately priced name readings in the second part: **Peter Benoit, Björn and Babylon**. The tonnage remains unresolved. The source reports intended movements; their completion and the port of departure are not established here.

### p213 A2

**Readable German — existing word repairs and shared J/Y interpretation, with three historical ship-name proposals:**

> Weitere Tonnage folgt baldigst. Ferner Rohstofftransport abging heute Peter Benoit. Folgt morgen Bjoern und Babylon.

The names can be compared with contemporary shipping sources. *Lloyd's
Register*, **1917–18**, lists **Peter Benoit** at PES–PET, entry P471, and
three vessels named **Björn** at BJE–BLA, entries B733–735. A shipping notice
in the *Hamburger Fremdenblatt*, **28 December 1915**, evening edition,
printed p3, names the steamer **Babylon**.

| Received field | Name proposal | Extra observed-coordinate changes under the existing J/Y layer |
|---|---|---:|
| `PETERXBENVIT` | **Peter Benoit** | 2 |
| `B9VERN` → conditional `BJVERN` | **Bjoern** | 2 |
| `BAC4LON` → conditional `BACYLON` | **Babylon** | 2 |

These sources establish the spellings, not the November transport identities.
The three Björn entries make a unique vessel identification especially
uncertain. No same-movement witness has been found. Accepting all three
proposals gives the quotation above at **nine observed substitutions and
one source-mask fill**, six substitutions beyond the earlier word edition.
It uses the existing **GD=J** and **DD=Y** hypotheses without another key
assignment. No previously unknown plaintext position is added to the count.

[Register and newspaper crops, exact name costs and source provenance](../../experiments/reval_ship_name_comparison/README.md).

## Heated sick wagons, cooking equipment and hot tea

**Sources on this page:** p213 A6, p213 A7. [Concise case study](../military/medical_return_transports.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p212 A1](212.md#source-p212-a1), [p212 A5](212.md#source-p212-a5).

<a id="edition-cases-military-medical-return-transports-heated-sick-wagons-cooking-equipment-and-hot-tea"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs pp212–213, 22 November 1918; published `Nov22-24` key, unchanged. [Inputs](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/inputs.json), [exact certificates](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/certificates.json), [method and limits](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/README.md).

The readable medical passages concern preparations for transports coming through from Turkey. They recommend a sick wagon fitted with stoves, cooking equipment and continuously available hot tea. The final paragraph asks for action as far as possible from Constantinople because the received place `NIKOLA9EW` may lack sufficient capacity. The text records recommendations and a forwarding request, not proof that the equipment or supplies were provided.

The source has a nominal seven-part frame. Parts 2 and 4 were retained as unassigned context in this medical package and are excluded from its restored-reading count. A subsequent [cross-copy audit](../caucasus/p212_p218_crosscopy.md) identifies the printed part 2 as a truncated copy of a separate Caucasus/Russia withdrawal message on p218. The [conditional part-4 edition](../military/p212_medical_fragment.md) now recovers 129/151 positions in its primary reading and 148/151 in an optional transport-doctor reading. The latter fills 102 missing coordinates without changing an observed coordinate; the 302-coordinate frame remains a hypothesis, and three opening positions remain unresolved. An unnumbered oil-cartel query between them is [edited separately](../finance/oil_cartel_dispatch_query.md). The relation of the seven printed parts remains unresolved.

**The gap location is not unique.** All 340 possible single five-coordinate gaps were checked against the recorded candidate. Gaps 104, 105, 107 and 108 tie at nine observed-coordinate changes. All four raw variants and exact repair certificates remain available; the proposed reading is conditional and is not described as a uniquely restored source.

<a id="edition-cases-military-medical-return-transports-attribution-and-retained-gaps"></a>

### Attribution and retained gaps

The sick-wagon and final medical passages already had recognizable unreviewed repository candidates. This edition records the exact source and all local repairs; it makes no first historical decipherment claim. The two initially unassigned frames and all four tied first-part geometries remain preserved in this package's frozen evidence; the later part-2 identification has its own certificate and counting scope. No baseline square or later-period relabeling is applied to the medical readings.
